Task: Sanitize PyYAML constructor failures in load_config
Description: config.load_config catches only yaml.YAMLError, but PyYAML's construction stage raises whatever Python raised at it: an out-of-range implicit timestamp (2026-02-30) raises ValueError, !!bool <junk> raises KeyError(<the value>), !!timestamp <junk> raises AttributeError, and deep flow nesting raises RecursionError. Two of those put file content in the message, so a secret pasted into config.yaml reaches the terminal in an unhandled traceback. Same defect and same fix as the one closed in research/allowlist.py at M1-308 round 7; found there, filed here because it is pre-existing on the diff base.
Acceptance Criteria: load_config translates every non-YAMLError failure of yaml.safe_load into a sanitized ConfigError raised from None; no value from the file appears in the message or the cause chain; regression tests cover the invalid implicit timestamp, the !!bool/!!int/!!timestamp explicit-tag shapes and deep flow nesting.
Source or Decision Reference: M1-308 round-7 review; CLAUDE.md error hygiene

Task: Gut the questions package __init__ re-export block
Description: questions/__init__.py re-exports every submodule, so importing whiskeyjack_bot.questions.model -- the canonical question schema, which imports no SDK itself -- transitively loads forecasting_tools, asknews_sdk, litellm, httpx and streamlit. Same defect and same fix as the one closed in research/__init__.py at M1-308 round 4, where it cost verify-env 7.0s and three stray warnings; gutting it there took the import to 0.204s. Pre-existing on master with no live symptom today (env_verify and cli import no canonical question, and test_env_verify.py's subprocess probe fails if that changes). Found while building M1-402, whose forecast/inputs.py inherits the coupling and documents it rather than fixing a merged module on a review branch.
Acceptance Criteria: questions/__init__.py holds a one-line docstring and no re-exports; a fresh interpreter importing whiskeyjack_bot.questions.model loads none of forecasting_tools, asknews_sdk, litellm, httpx or streamlit; every existing importer of the removed names is updated to the submodule path; the four gates stay green.

Task: Harden the AskNews adapter's caller preflight
Description: Refuse malformed caller arguments before any billable AskNews call, matching the Exa adapter's round-4 preflight.
Acceptance Criteria: A bare string of queries and malformed run metadata are refused with the module's own error and zero provider calls; the preflight is shared with the Exa adapter rather than copied.

Task: Decide the terminal DNS root dot in canonicalize_url
Description: canonicalize_url preserves a terminal root dot, so https://bls.gov./x and https://bls.gov/x are two dedup keys for one page. M1-303 normalizes it locally for official-domain matching; the canonical form itself is document identity and is not changed on a review branch.
Acceptance Criteria: Either canonicalize_url normalizes one terminal root dot and the identity change is recorded, or the dot is documented as identity-bearing with a rationale; dedup collapses the two spellings of one host iff that decision says it should.

Description: exa.retrieve_web refuses a single-label include_domains entry ("com", "gov") because it would fake official attribution for every registrable domain under it, but a multi-label public suffix ("co.uk", "com.au") is still accepted. Stated as a known residual in M1-303 rather than half-fixed on a review branch.
Acceptance Criteria: include_domains rejects public suffixes, including multi-label suffixes such as co.uk and com.au, before any provider call, while accepting registrable domains and their subdomains.

Task: Compose artifact and ledger persistence for a paid run
Description: research.store and research.artifacts are separate primitives, so the ordering rule that keeps a paid run recordable when its artifact write fails - write the artifact first, then persist the ledger row with raw_response_path NULL - lives only in a docstring and in the caller. M1-306 deliberately shipped the primitives without the composition, because the composed entry point belongs with the retrieval orchestrator that item does not ship.
Acceptance Criteria: One paid-result persistence API attempts artifact storage and still commits the run and its documents with raw_response_path NULL after an ordinary artifact I/O failure, and reports the audit loss to its caller rather than swallowing it.

Description: ResearchPacket is a frozen dataclass holding tuples of pydantic models, so its digest is stable against rebinding its fields but not against mutating a caller-retained run, document, query list or provider-config dict after build_packet returns. No current product path mutates a packet after construction, so this is a hardening item rather than a live defect.
Acceptance Criteria: After build_packet returns, mutation of caller-owned runs, documents, lists or provider-config dictionaries cannot change the packet's digest; a property test asserts the digest is unchanged after mutating each mutable input.

Task: Refuse an unusable artifact path as the module's own error
Description: research/artifacts.py::read_raw_responses catches OSError around path.read_bytes(), but a lone surrogate in the relative path raises UnicodeEncodeError (a ValueError) out of open() before any I/O, so a raw exception escapes a public boundary -- the class of defect this project has taken as a review finding twice. Found by M1-406's property suite against its own sibling reader (forecast/artifacts.py), where it was closed on that branch; the same hole in the merged retrieval reader is pre-existing and is filed rather than fixed cross-item. Reachable without a hostile operator: research_runs.raw_response_path is a TEXT column whose shape nothing constrains, and read_raw_responses is a public entry point taking a caller-supplied string. The message must not render the path, because interpolating it is itself the failing operation.
Acceptance Criteria: read_raw_responses raises ArtifactError, not UnicodeEncodeError, for a relative_path carrying a lone surrogate; the message names no path; a property asserts that only ArtifactError escapes the reader on arbitrary input, and fails against the pre-fix code.

Task: Cross-check the configured probability bounds against the prompt
Description: forecast.min_probability and forecast.max_probability are enforced against model output by M1-403, while prompts/forecaster.md prints 0.001-0.999 to the model as a literal. Nothing compares the two, so narrowing the config silently asks for a probability the prompt never permits and pays for a repair turn to discover it. M1-403 made the divergence observable rather than creating it, so it is a row and not a fix on that branch.
Acceptance Criteria: A config whose probability bounds fall outside the range the loaded prompt declares is reported at startup and by verify-env, before any billable call; the check reads the prompt that config actually names rather than a copy of its numbers.

Description: Require prior/base rate, status quo, evidence links, load-bearing facts, failure modes and final output.

Description: Use NumericDistribution.from_question and get_cdf to produce the submission array.
Acceptance Criteria: Exactly 201 monotone values for normal numeric questions; maintained PMF constraint passes.

Description: Flag or fail according to config before approval.
Acceptance Criteria: No-sources and stale-only fixtures produce explicit states and never pass silently.

Task: Enforce the prompt's evidence caps against document provenance
Description: prompts/forecaster.md caps what a document may justify by its reliability_tag and provenance: an unverified_social document "may justify a tiny or small adjustment at most, never a load-bearing fact", and an llm_reported one is capped at small unless the cited account is official_primary or a direct_api document corroborates it. The response schema carries direction, magnitude and load_bearing, and M1-501 resolves every citation to a supplied source_id -- but a source_id is only an identity, so nothing compares a claimed magnitude against the reliability of the document it cites. A forecast can still rest a load-bearing fact on a single unverified social post and be recorded as valid. Enforcing the caps needs the documents themselves (ForecastDocumentInput.reliability_tag/provenance), not just their ids, which is a wider input than M1-501's checker takes and a rule the prompt states rather than one this project would be inventing. Raised while implementing M1-501.
Acceptance Criteria: An evidence adjustment or load-bearing fact whose citations are all documents the prompt caps below the claimed magnitude is refused as a repairable sanitized problem before the forecast is recorded; a corroborating direct_api citation lifts the llm_reported cap exactly as the prompt states, and no message echoes document content.

Task: Expose one composed output-validation entry point
Description: The output checks a valid forecast must pass are split across modules on purpose -- attribution.attribution_problems (cross-type, M1-501), binary.binary_output_problems (M1-403), and the option-set and percentile-level checks M1-404 and M1-405 will add. generate._output_problems composes them, but it is private to the call path, so a caller that is NOT generating -- M1-406 replaying a stored response, M1-602 validating a record before it is persisted -- has to know the full list and call each one. Nothing tells it when that list grows. M1-501's round-1 cross-model review reported a missing binary-prior check against attribution.py for exactly this reason: reading one checker in isolation, the rule looks absent. The rule was present in binary.py and the composed path refuses the response (reproduced by execution, rebutted in round 2), but a seam that misleads a careful reader is a seam a caller will get wrong.
Acceptance Criteria: One public entry point returns every output problem for a response of any supported question type, composing the cross-type and type-specific checkers; generate._output_problems is defined in terms of it rather than beside it, so the two cannot diverge; a test fails if a supported question type has a checker the entry point does not reach.

Task: Run the composed output validation on the persist path
Description: forecast/store.py never imports ForecastConfig and never calls the composed output-validation entry point: _require_attributable runs attribution.validate_attribution_fields alone, so append_forecast_version validates the cross-type attribution rules but not the type-specific ones. A record whose probability falls outside the configured forecast.min_probability/max_probability can therefore be persisted, and since M1-405 so can a numeric record whose percentiles are not the declared nine, are out of order, or fall outside the question's bounds -- even though the generating path refuses both. The two entry points disagree about what a valid forecast is. Not reachable from the product path today: forecast.generate runs the full composed check inside its attempt loop before anything reaches the writer, so every record stored by persist_generation was already checked. It is reachable by any other caller of the public writer, and the gap widens again when M1-404 adds the option-set checker. M1-405 shrank what closing it costs: validate.output_problems now takes a CanonicalQuestion rather than a bare question_id, and ForecastRecordDraft.question already carries one validated to agree with the row, so only ForecastConfig still has to be threaded. That is still a signature change to a merged and reviewed public entry point, which is why M1-506 filed this rather than fixing it -- same convention as M1-314, M2-709 and M1-608.
Acceptance Criteria: append_forecast_version runs the same composed output-validation entry point forecast.generate runs, so the accepted response sets of the two paths are equal; a test drives one out-of-bounds probability and one malformed percentile set through both and asserts both refuse them; the refusal stays a ForecastRecordError naming no stored value.

Description: Give research and generation failures an attempt-scoped ledger identity: they occur before any forecast_records row exists, so migration 003's forecast-scoped lifecycle_events cannot hold them. Needs migration 004.
Acceptance Criteria: A research or generation failure with no forecast record still produces a queryable ledger event; the failed attempt is linked to the forecast version that later succeeds for the same question.
Source or Decision Reference: D25; CODEX_HANDOFF pipeline and failure boundaries

Task: Apply the non-blank identifier guard to the pre-004 identifier columns
Description: Migration 004 and lifecycle._require_identifier refuse a blank or blob attempt_id on both ends of the attempt->forecast join. The identifier columns that shipped before it -- forecast_records.record_id, submission_attempts.attempt_id and idempotency_key, research_runs.retrieval_run_id -- have no such guard: _require_text refuses '' but '\n\t' is truthy and reaches storage, and one-argument trim() in 001/003 strips U+0020 alone. Pre-existing, so M1-606 scoped its fix to its own writer rather than widening a shared validator under already-reviewed code.
Acceptance Criteria: A whitespace-only or blob identifier is refused at every writer and every trigger that takes one, with the same 29-codepoint whitespace set 003 pinned; a test asserts the writer and trigger definitions agree over every codepoint Python calls whitespace.
Source or Decision Reference: D25; M1-606 M1-NOTES deviation; M1-603 round 5

Task: Pin the shared identifier bound between lifecycle and approval
Description: approval._MAX_IDENTIFIER restates lifecycle._MAX_IDENTIFIER (both 200) with no pinned relationship. approval.py deliberately does not import lifecycle's private validators -- they raise the wrong error type -- so the bound was respelled, and a future change to either constant would silently let the two entry points accept different record_id sets. Behaviour agrees at this revision, so this is a hardening item rather than a live defect.
Acceptance Criteria: Approval and lifecycle entry points derive the record_id length limit from one public contract; a test asserts the two accepted input sets cannot diverge if that limit changes.

Task: Give the record schema the identifier shape rule every other layer applies
Description: forecast/record.py's identifier fields (record_id, tournament_id, attempt_id, retrieval_run_id) carry Field(min_length=1, max_length=MAX_IDENTIFIER_LENGTH) and nothing else. Every other layer that touches those columns -- lifecycle, approval, submission, submission_gateway, submission_live, and 006/007/008's triggers -- also refuses a whitespace-only value and one bearing a NUL, because min_length=1 admits '\n\t' and a blank identity is an unjoinable row on an append-only table. M1-608 pinned the length to bounds.MAX_IDENTIFIER_LENGTH across all six modules and found this while doing it, but closing it would change what a merged, reviewed pydantic model accepts -- the behaviour-change-to-merged-code M1-606 refused to smuggle in under a different item, and the same convention M1-507, M1-314 and M2-709 were filed under. Not reachable from the product path today: forecast/store.py's writer goes through lifecycle's validators before any row is inserted, and 006 refuses the value at the schema regardless, so what a caller building a record by hand gets today is a constraint failure rather than a field-level message.
Acceptance Criteria: ForecastRecord and ForecastRecordDraft refuse a whitespace-only or NUL-bearing identifier with a ForecastRecordError naming the field and no stored value; a test drives the model and 006's triggers over the same candidate set and asserts the accepted sets are equal, in the shape tests/unit/test_shared_bounds.py already uses for the length bound.

Description: Approve or reject the exact forecast hash as append-only events.
Acceptance Criteria: Changed forecast invalidates prior approval; actor/timestamp/note are retained.

Description: Derive keys from tournament, question, forecast version and payload hash.
Acceptance Criteria: Same payload/key cannot create two attempts; changed payload requires a new approval/key.

Acceptance Criteria: Dry run records payload/hash and makes zero HTTP post calls.

Acceptance Criteria: Success requires refetch confirmation; uncertain timeout blocks blind retry.

Description: Decide whether refetch receipt is sufficient or add a contract-tested narrow HTTP adapter.
Acceptance Criteria: Decision and test evidence recorded; no private package method dependency without a guard.

Description: Submit one explicit owner-approved test forecast and persist receipt/refetch.
Acceptance Criteria: Forecast appears on bot profile; ledger has approval, payload, attempt and verification snapshot.

Task: Bind an approval to the submission payload it authorized
Description: An approval binds to forecast_sha256, so one approved forecast covers every payload built from it: a payload that changed without the forecast changing gets a new idempotency key (M2-702) while keeping its old approval in force. M2-702 ships the half it can -- submission_key_for_approved_record refuses a record with no approval -- but cannot check that a payload IS the one the approval meant, because the forecast->payload mapping does not exist until M1-502/M1-503. Raised by M2-702 round-1 cross-model review; reading recorded as D33.
Acceptance Criteria: A submission payload that does not derive from the approved forecast is refused before any post; the binding is append-only and an operator can see what a decision authorized.

Task: Reserve an idempotency key atomically before any post
Description: submission.require_key_unused() is a read and says so: two concurrent commands can both see one key as unused, and 001's UNIQUE constraint only refuses the second row AFTER its post has been made. Nothing is reachable today -- no gateway exists -- but the post-call insert cannot by itself prevent a duplicate live post. Raised as a backlog candidate by M2-702 round-1 cross-model review.
Acceptance Criteria: Two concurrent commands for the same derived key durably select one poster before any network I/O; the loser posts nothing, and every completed call remains recordable.

Task: Share one atomic never-overwrite artifact writer
Description: research/artifacts._write_new_file and submission_gateway._write_or_confirm are the same mkstemp+fsync+os.link mechanism written twice, because the first is private to its module and raises ArtifactError. The duplication is deliberate for M2-703 -- extracting a shared helper changes a merged, reviewed module and belongs to its own item -- but a second copy of a race-sensitive write is exactly the kind of code that drifts. The two differ on purpose in one place (a dry-run destination whose bytes match is a no-op; a retrieval artifact is always a collision), so the shared helper has to take that as a parameter rather than pick one behaviour.
Acceptance Criteria: One atomic create-or-fail helper is used by both artifact writers; each keeps its own error type; a test drives the EEXIST path of both through the shared code.

Task: Refuse an identifier the ledger cannot store when deriving a key
Description: submission._require_text accepts a whitespace-only or NUL-bearing tournament_id, and 006_non_blank_identifiers.sql refuses one -- so submission_key() will mint a key for a tournament no forecast_records row can hold. Not reachable from a product path today: config.py's TournamentConfig already refuses a blank slug, and submission_key_for_record reads the value back out of a row 006 has already vetted. It surfaced as a flaky property test (test_a_key_survives_the_store_and_load_round_trip stores what it draws, and the dev profile is randomized), whose strategy was narrowed on the M2-703 branch so the gate is deterministic. Same class as M1-608: two spellings of one bound, agreeing at this revision by coincidence rather than by construction.
Acceptance Criteria: submission.py's identifier validator refuses exactly what 006's triggers refuse; a test drives both layers over the same inputs and asserts the accepted sets are equal; the narrowed property strategy is restored.

Task: Record a submission whose outcome is unknown
Description: lifecycle.record_submission_attempt derives its event from (success, verified_by_refetch), and that pair has no member meaning "the post raised AND the refetch could not be performed". (False, False) is submission_failed, which is terminal and claims the post did not go through -- more than is known. M2-704 makes the cell rare by retrying the refetch and says so in the row's error_message, and terminal failed is at least the conservative direction, but the ledger asserts something it cannot support. Closing it needs a vocabulary member and therefore a migration, so it is a filed item rather than an M2-704 change. Raised by M2-704 during implementation.
Acceptance Criteria: A post whose outcome no refetch established is recorded as neither submitted nor failed; the record stays somewhere a later refetch can still resolve it, and a test drives the post-raised/refetch-unreadable pair through both layers.

Acceptance Criteria: One live forecast succeeds once; complete pre-resolution record and verified receipt exist.

Acceptance Criteria: Resolved fixture updates only via append event; annulled/ambiguous outcomes are not scored.

Description: Record platform numeric/log/peer scores instead of claiming an unverified local replica.
Acceptance Criteria: Numeric record identifies score source and does not label a proxy as Metaculus score.

Acceptance Criteria: Export contains counts, calibration bins and score summaries with small-sample warnings.

Acceptance Criteria: No live network calls in CI; uncertain-outcome path blocks duplicate submit.

Acceptance Criteria: One command produces one validated record, zero provider calls and zero submission calls.

Acceptance Criteria: Golden edge cases pass on 0.2.92; dependency drift triggers a visible failure.

Acceptance Criteria: Another operator can recover from each failure state without editing the database.

Acceptance Criteria: Every table/field and export version has an auditable definition.

Acceptance Criteria: Bot profile exists; token works in verify-env and is absent from repository/history.

Acceptance Criteria: Verified LiteLLM model name completes one structured fixture call within cost cap.

Acceptance Criteria: verify-env recognizes keys; one citation-retaining test query succeeds.

Acceptance Criteria: XAI_API_KEY is present in the operator environment and current X Search pricing is recorded in Verified Facts; retrieval.social stays disabled until both hold.

Task: Verify SQLite foreign-key enforcement after connection setup
Description: ledger.connect sets PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON but never reads it back, unlike journal_mode and recursive_triggers, which are both read back and raise LedgerError when the setting did not take. An unknown or ignored PRAGMA is a silent no-op in SQLite, so foreign-key enforcement is assumed rather than verified. M1-607 relies on that assumption: it guards the five identifier primary keys directly and leaves every FK column (the four *_forecast_record_id columns, forecast_records/research_documents.retrieval_run_id) covered transitively. Declared there as a standing risk rather than fixed, because reading the PRAGMA back changes ledger.connect's contract and belongs to its own item. Raised as a non-blocking backlog candidate by M1-607 cross-model review round 1.
Acceptance Criteria: ledger.connect reads PRAGMA foreign_keys back and raises LedgerError unless it is enabled, with a message naming the path and no stored value; a test asserts the refusal, and the existing journal_mode/recursive_triggers read-backs are the shape to follow. Note in the item that no deterministic failure is reproducible on the supported SQLite runtime -- the PRAGMA is recognized and set outside a transaction -- so this closes an unverified assumption rather than a demonstrated defect.
Source or Decision Reference: M1-607 review round 1 (non-blocking); M1-607 M1-NOTES standing risk

Task: Stop treating include_input=False as a sufficient pydantic sanitizer
Description: Five modules rebuild a pydantic ValidationError with errors(include_input=False, include_url=False) and the codebase has been reading that as "the offending value cannot escape". It is not sufficient, on two counts, both reproduced by execution during M1-602's round-1 remediation. (1) Several of pydantic's own msg strings interpolate the input into the message text, which the flags do not touch: a union_tag_invalid error reads "Input tag 'X' found using 'k' does not match ...", and X is the untrusted value. (2) Under extra="forbid" the loc of an unexpected key IS that key, so a stored or provider-supplied object leaks its key names through the field path. forecast/schema.py and research/model.py already guard (2) with a schema-authored field-name set; config.py, research/allowlist.py and questions/normalize.py render err['msg'] and are not guarded against (1). No merged module has a reachable leak today -- the only discriminated-union adapter in src/ (CanonicalQuestionAdapter) is defined and never called -- so this is a latent hazard and a false rule, not a live defect. M1-602 closed both halves in forecast/record.py; the rule needs stating once and applying everywhere, before the next module adds a union.
Acceptance Criteria: One shared sanitizer renders a ValidationError from loc and type only, withholding any loc part the schema did not author; every module that catches a ValidationError uses it; a test plants a marker in both a value and a key at top level and nested and asserts neither reaches the message, and a companion test asserts an authored field name still survives so the withholding is not blanket.

Task: Decide what a tied percentile value may cost on the conversion path
Description: prompts/forecaster.md tells the model percentile values must be non-decreasing, and M1-405 enforces exactly that: two equal values are a reply that followed the prompt, and refusing one would spend the single budgeted repair call on the project's own inconsistency. The pinned SDK agrees at the declared stage -- NumericDistribution._check_percentiles_increasing raises only on value[i] > value[i+1] -- but then _check_and_update_repeating_values MUTATES declared_percentiles in place, nudging every repeated value by 1e-6 when it is inside the bounds and by 1e-10 when it is at or outside one. That runs inside the model_validator, so it happens on construction, before get_cdf is ever called. The record stores the percentiles the model returned; the CDF submitted would be built from values this project did not produce and does not persist. Against 'nothing is clamped' (binary.py, M1-502's 'no arbitrary post-hoc renormalization is hidden') that is a real divergence, and it is invisible unless someone reads the SDK. Not a defect in M1-405: the nudge happens in the conversion M1-503 owns, and the options -- record the nudged values as a derived artifact, refuse ties at the conversion boundary, or bump the prompt to ask for strictly increasing values and re-hash -- are all M1-503's or the prompt owner's to weigh. UPDATE (M1-503): this is no longer only an attribution question. The same rewrite can make the converted percentile set non-monotone, which drives forecasting-tools 0.2.92's _standardize_cdf into a non-terminating scale search -- see M1-514 for the mechanism and M1-503's forecast/cdf.py for the guard now in place.
Acceptance Criteria: A tied percentile value either cannot reach NumericDistribution, or the difference between the declared percentiles and the ones the submitted CDF was built from is recorded rather than silent; a test constructs the tie and asserts the chosen behaviour against the pinned SDK by execution. Whichever branch is taken must also leave M1-503's liveness guard intact or replace it: M1-503 found that a repeated value at or beyond a bound is rewritten ONTO that bound, which can leave the converted set non-monotone and send _standardize_cdf's scale search into a loop with no exit (M1-514). Recording the divergence alone does not close this row while a tie can still hang the conversion.

Task: Settle whether a configured probability bound may be rendered in a diagnostic
Description: binary.binary_output_problems renders forecast.min_probability and forecast.max_probability into its out-of-bounds message, and M1-403 argued for it: prompts/forecaster.md prints 0.001-0.999 to the model as a literal while config is free to narrow it, so a repair turn that does not state the actual bound is one no model can satisfy. That argument is specific and it still holds. What is not settled is the category. CLAUDE.md's error-hygiene rule says a message never echoes stored, file or field values, and names filesystem paths as the ONE carve-out -- config values are not paths. The string also does not stop at the repair turn: after a second failure it reaches ForecastGeneration.failure_problems and from there the persisted raw-output artifact. M1-405 hit the same question for numeric and resolved it the other way, because there the model is already sent the bounds (forecast/inputs.py) so naming them back buys nothing -- which is attribution.py's argument for not rendering supplied source_ids. Binary genuinely differs, so the two modules now differ on purpose rather than by accident, and that difference should be written down as a decision or removed. Raised as a non-blocking observation by M1-405's round-1 cross-model review, which classed it pre-existing: this branch adds binary's question parameter and does not increase the pattern's reachability or impact. **Widened by M1-502 round-1 cross-model review (2026-08-28): this is not binary's alone.** forecast/multiple_choice.py renders the same configured pair -- its per-option bounds problem is built as "each probability must be between {low!r} and {high!r} inclusive" -- so the two categorical checkers agree with each other and the row's framing of binary as the lone outlier was wrong. M1-502 added tests that assert those exact strings, which pins the current behaviour but decides nothing. The envelope check M1-502 added alongside them deliberately withholds the configured pair and names only the spec's 0.001/0.999 ends, so the module is now internally inconsistent on purpose, pending this row.
Acceptance Criteria: Either the configured bounds stop appearing in categorical diagnostics -- binary AND multiple-choice -- and the repair turn is shown to stay actionable without them, or the carve-out is widened in CLAUDE.md to name operator-supplied configuration values alongside paths and both modules cite it. Tests pin whichever holds, in both modules, and forecast/numeric.py's value-free messages stop disagreeing with them silently.
Source or Decision Reference: M1-405 round-1 cross-model review; D11; M1-401 path carve-out; M1-502 round-1 cross-model review

Task: Make the composed output-validation properties registry-complete
Description: M1-405 round 3 found that composed_cases() in tests/property/test_forecast_properties.py generates only binary and multiple-choice responses, though _TYPE_CHECKERS now registers three non-None checkers. _type_specific_half dispatches through the registry, so the *dispatch* is complete, but the numeric checker is never reached through the composed entry point by any property: 300 draws produced 190 multiple_choice, 110 binary and 0 numeric. M1-405's own request claimed the opposite as risk 15 and the claim was false. No product defect follows -- section 5b covers numeric_output_problems directly -- but this is the project's top recurring defect class (a property that cannot fail for the branch it names) reappearing one level up: here the guard's dispatch is registry-driven while the strategy that feeds it is not, so the anti-vacuity guard is itself partly vacuous. It will silently worsen with each new registration.
Acceptance Criteria: Every non-None _TYPE_CHECKERS entry is generated by the composed strategy, with an anti-vacuity assertion that fails when any registered response type is absent from the draws -- so a fourth registration cannot silently go uncovered. The numeric arm must reach both a biting and a silent verdict, event-tagged like the existing arms.

Task: Decide whether the option count is capped at generation as well as at post time
Description: submission_live._MAX_CATEGORIES refuses a multiple-choice payload naming more than 64 options, and that bound is this module's own rather than the platform's: it is what keeps a verification snapshot inside _MAX_BODY. forecast/multiple_choice.py has no such cap, so a 65-option reply is validated, recorded, approved and only then refused -- one billed call plus an approval decision spent on a post that cannot happen. That is exactly the ordering argument the owner accepted for per-option bounds (M1-404, 2026-08-26): a repair turn at generation costs one call against a live post that never lands. M1-404 rejected the cap anyway, and the counter-argument is equally specific -- a cap this project invented would refuse a question Metaculus accepted, and _MAX_CATEGORIES is a serialization budget, not a platform limit. The two arguments are both right and they point opposite ways, which is why this is a decision rather than a defect. Raised while implementing M1-502.
Acceptance Criteria: Either the generating path refuses an option count no post could carry and cites the bound it is deriving that from, or the asymmetry is recorded as a decision naming why a serialization budget must not become a forecast rule; a test pins whichever holds, and forecast/multiple_choice.py and submission_live.py stop disagreeing silently.
Source or Decision Reference: M1-502; M1-404 per-option bounds owner decision

Task: Refuse a bounds/option-count pair that no multiple-choice reply can satisfy
Description: multiple_choice_output_problems requires every option probability to be at least forecast.min_probability AND the vector to sum to 1 within 1e-6. For a question carrying n options those two rules are jointly satisfiable only while n <= 1 / min_probability -- 1000 at the committed default. Past that, every reply is refused, the repair turn asks for something no model can produce, and the question costs two billed calls to fail. This is the same class binary._require_config already refuses for an inverted bounds pair, and generate_forecast already runs two such preflights before spending (the bounds pair and M1-405's zero_point check), so the shape of the fix is settled. It is filed rather than built because it is not reachable today: Metaculus multiple-choice questions carry a few dozen options, which submission_live._MAX_CATEGORIES records at 64. It becomes reachable if a narrower min_probability is ever configured -- at 0.05 the ceiling is 20 options. Raised while implementing M1-502.
Acceptance Criteria: A question whose option count and configured min_probability admit no valid distribution is refused before any billable call, as an error naming the configured bound and the count and no model output; a test drives one such pair and asserts client.calls == [].

Task: Make the probability envelope a true single source
Description: M1-502 round 1 moved the spec's 0.001-0.999 envelope into config.PROBABILITY_BOUND_FLOOR/CEILING and had forecast/binary.py, forecast/multiple_choice.py and forecast/generate.py's preflight re-check against those constants, closing the round-1 blocker. It did not go far enough, and M1-502's round-2 review said so: submission_live.py still declares its own executable 0.001 and 0.999, so there are two sources in src/ for one spec number and nothing fails if they drift. M1-502's risk claim 4 asserted a single source and was true only of the forecast package. The new diagnostics also embed the endpoints as literal strings in their messages rather than deriving them from the constants, so a change to the envelope would leave the message stating the old pair. Non-blocking on M1-502: the submission declarations predate both the branch and the pinned base, and the two sources agree today. Note this is deliberately NOT M1-509, which asks whether a *configured* pair may be rendered at all; this row is about the *spec* endpoints having one owner. Raised by M1-502 round-2 cross-model review.
Acceptance Criteria: Submission validation and forecast validation consume the same endpoint constants, and the diagnostics that name the envelope derive their displayed endpoints from those constants rather than from literal strings; a test fails if a second executable declaration of either endpoint appears in src/, so the two cannot drift silently.
Source or Decision Reference: M1-502 round-2 cross-model review; CODEX_HANDOFF.md Configuration schema

Task: Bound the numeric conversion in time
Description: forecasting-tools==0.2.92's NumericDistribution._standardize_cdf finds its scale factor with `lo = hi = scale = 1.0; while capped_sum(hi) < 1.0: hi *= 1.2`, where capped_sum sums min(cap, scale * pmf) over the interior points. A negative interior PMF entry makes that sum fall without bound as scale grows instead of rising, so hi reaches inf, inf * 1.2 is still inf, and capped_sum(inf) is -inf -- still below 1.0. The loop has no exit: get_cdf does not raise and is not slow, it never returns, and nothing on the forecast path imposes a deadline, so generate_forecast stops with no error, no failure event and no billing bound. Found on M1-503 by fuzzing the conversion under a worker-thread deadline. Two unrelated inputs reach it from replies numeric_output_problems accepts and prompts/forecaster.md asks for (it says non-decreasing, so a tie is compliant): a repeated value at or beyond a bound, which _check_and_update_repeating_values rewrites ONTO the bound while leaving an unrepeated value further out alone; and a log-scaled question whose values span many orders of magnitude, where the interpolation loses order with no rewrite involved. M1-503 ships the deterministic guard it can -- it evaluates the SDK's own pre-standardization curve via _get_cdf_at and refuses a set that is not non-decreasing with a positive span, which closes both known inputs and costs one extra interpolation -- but that guard is keyed on the mechanism it has evidence for, not on a proof that no other input diverges, and it reaches into a private SDK method. This row owns the general answer: a wall-clock bound on the conversion, or on the forecast path as a whole, so an unknown non-terminating input degrades to a recorded failure rather than a stopped run. Note M0-002 pins 0.2.92 and CI fails on drift, so upgrading past the defect is itself a decision rather than an action.
Acceptance Criteria: A numeric conversion that does not terminate is cut off and recorded as a pipeline failure rather than stopping the run; the bound is asserted by a test that constructs a non-terminating input and fails loudly instead of hanging the suite; M1-503's pre-standardization guard either remains as the fast path or is replaced, and whichever is chosen is stated with its reason.

Task: Compose the live paid forecast run
Description: T-903 shipped whiskeyjack_bot.pipeline.run_replay and the `run` CLI command, and both are replay-only by construction: no provider SDK, no HTTP client and no model client is reachable from that module's import graph, which is how its two zeroes (zero provider calls, zero submission calls) are pinned by a test rather than by a mock count. The paid composition is therefore still unwritten. It is the same split M1-312 made against M1-306 -- composing paid calls is a different risk from composing free ones -- and it is also where the two parts of CODEX_HANDOFF's `run` signature that T-903 deliberately did not implement belong: --limit and the batch loop over a snapshot's questions. A live run calls generate_forecast instead of replay_generation, must not repeat a paid retrieval when a later phase is retried, and needs the per-question failure isolation a batch loop implies, none of which the replay path exercises.
Acceptance Criteria: One command forecasts one or more snapshot questions through live retrieval and a live model call, writing one validated record per question; a per-question failure records its pipeline event and does not abort the batch; retrying a later phase repeats no paid call unless asked; the replay path's structural zero-provider-call guarantee is unchanged, which requires the paid composition to live outside whiskeyjack_bot.pipeline or that module's import-graph test to be restated.
Source or Decision Reference: T-903 module boundary; CODEX_HANDOFF Required CLI entry points

Task: Enforce AppConfig at the pipeline public boundary
Description: T-903's round-2 cross-model review classed this non-blocking and it is: the guards are private, the CLI always supplies load_config's AppConfig, and the behaviour predates the branch. It is still worth a row because T-903's own round-2 request claimed the opposite as risk claim 7 -- that _require_retained_output cannot be satisfied by a non-AppConfig -- and the claim was false: SimpleNamespace(storage=SimpleNamespace(retain_raw_model_output=True)) passes it, because the guard reads the attribute and checks the value's type rather than the object's. _require_replay_enabled has the same shape and the same hole, and it was written first, so this is a pattern rather than one slip: every AttributeError-to-PipelineError guard in pipeline.py says 'config must be an AppConfig' in its message while checking something weaker. The message is the part that is wrong -- either the check should match it or it should stop claiming a type it does not verify. Same defect class as the vacuous-property findings this project keeps hitting: a guard whose stated claim is stronger than what it can fail on.
Acceptance Criteria: run_replay refuses a non-AppConfig at the public boundary before any I/O, with one check whose failure message matches what it actually verifies; a test constructs a structurally compatible stand-in (SimpleNamespace or equivalent) and asserts it is refused, and the per-attribute guards inside pipeline.py either become that check or stop naming AppConfig in their messages.

Task: Give a post-generation persistence failure a ledger identity
Description: M1-315's live batch has three per-question failure shapes and only two of them can be written down. pipeline_failure_events.event_type is CHECK-constrained to ('research_failed','generation_failed'), and when a good forecast is refused by the ledger neither is true -- the generation succeeded. M1-315 therefore writes nothing for that case, reports it as status='not_recorded' with the sanitized reason on the batch result, and leaves the raw-output artifact on disk as the only durable trace. That is the honest choice under T-903's rule that a failure which did not happen must not be recorded, but it means the one failure mode that implies a sick ledger is the one the ledger does not see. Widening the vocabulary is a CHECK rebuild of an append-only table (the cost 009 refused), so it is a row rather than a sideways fix.
Acceptance Criteria: A forecast that generated successfully and could not be persisted leaves a durable, queryable record of that fact; the chosen mechanism does not weaken the append-only guarantee and does not require a forecast_records row that does not exist; a test drives a ledger refusal between the row and its validation event and asserts the record of the failure survives the process.

Task: Decide how retrieval queries are constructed from a question
Description: M1-315 needed queries and nothing in the tree derived them -- both adapters take a caller-supplied list and research/asknews.py says so ('deriving them from a question is not this item's job'). derive_queries ships the minimum that is defensible offline: the question title, plus the group parent title joined to it for an M1-202 sibling whose own title is a bare option label. It reads no config and is pure. This is the largest single lever on run cost -- retrieval.max_queries_per_question is 6 and AskNews bills two calls per query, so the committed ceiling is 12 billable calls per question against the 1 or 2 this produces. Whether that is the right trade is an empirical question this project cannot answer offline, and the alternatives were rejected without evidence: asking the model to expand the question spends a billable call to decide how to spend billable calls, and keyword heuristics over a title are guesses nothing here can evaluate.
Acceptance Criteria: Query construction is chosen against measured retrieval quality rather than by default, with the cost of each option stated in billable calls per question; whichever is chosen stays a pure function with a property pass; if the model is used to expand queries, the call is counted and recorded on the run like any other paid call.

Description: exa.decide_fallback takes official_source_required as one of its two authorizing triggers, and M1-315's orchestrator passes it False unconditionally -- because v1 config has no field that expresses a per-question official-source requirement and inventing one in the orchestrator would put a paid-call trigger in a module that cannot say where it came from. The consequence is that half of D18's policy is currently unreachable: the fallback runs only when AskNews fails. M1-304's structured-source router is where the requirement is supposed to originate.
Acceptance Criteria: A question that needs an official or authoritative source reaches decide_fallback with official_source_required=True from a source that can be pointed at, not from a literal; a test drives one such question and asserts the fallback ran with official_source_required among the persisted reasons.

Task: Move MissingCredentialError out of the module that holds the poster
Description: research/exa.py imports MissingCredentialError from metaculus/client.py, which also holds SingleAttemptPoster and build_poster. So importing the Exa adapter -- and therefore any live retrieval path -- puts the Metaculus posting client on the import graph, for an exception class. M1-315's guard on pipeline_live has to name that coupling explicitly instead of forbidding metaculus.client, which makes its claim weaker than the replay path's for a reason unrelated to what either module does. Not a live defect: posting still requires an approved record and a separate command. It is an import-graph guarantee that cannot be stated as simply as it should be.
Acceptance Criteria: MissingCredentialError lives in a module that holds no network client; every current importer is updated; a fresh interpreter importing whiskeyjack_bot.pipeline_live loads no Metaculus posting code, and the M1-315 guard forbids metaculus.client outright rather than documenting an exception to itself.

Task: Decide what a cross-provider duplicate document means to the forecaster
Description: dedup.dedup_key is (retrieval_run_id, canonical_url, content_sha256), so two runs can never collapse against each other by construction -- an article retrieved by both AskNews and Exa becomes two rows, two packet documents and two source ids, and forecast/inputs.py shows the model both. Dropping one would be an attribution loss (a run's row would claim evidence the packet does not carry), so M1-315 does not collapse them, but the model can double-count one article as two independent sources and the prompt's evidence rules read corroboration off distinct source ids. Bounded in practice, because M1-315's fallback runs mainly when the primary failed and therefore retained little.
Acceptance Criteria: A document retrieved by more than one provider is presented to the forecaster in a way that does not read as independent corroboration, without any run losing the claim that it retrieved it; a test builds a packet whose two runs share one canonical URL and content hash and asserts the chosen behaviour at the model-input boundary.
Source or Decision Reference: M1-305 dedup_key; M1-315 orchestrate module docstring

Task: Make gate.sh fail when a gate fails
Description: scripts/gate.sh reports 'FAIL', prints the failing output, says 'the remaining gates were not run' -- and exits 0. run_gate reads `status=$?` on the line after `fi`, and in bash an `if` whose condition is false and which has no `else` completes with status 0, so the captured status is the compound statement's, not the failing command's, and `exit "$status"` exits clean. Verified by execution on the M1-315 branch: a deliberately misformatted file makes gate.sh print the ruff format failure and return 0. The human-readable output is correct, so a person reading the terminal is not misled; anything reading the exit code is. That is the failure mode docs/LESSONS.md lesson 7 names -- a check whose failure mode is a silent pass -- in the script whose whole purpose is to be the check. Not currently load-bearing for a review request: review-request.py runs the four gates itself through subprocess and tests returncode, so its refusal-on-red is unaffected. It is load-bearing for any hook, wrapper or CI step that shells out to gate.sh, and for a session that reads the exit code instead of the text. Found while remediating M1-315 round 1.
Acceptance Criteria: scripts/gate.sh exits non-zero whenever any of the four gates fails, with the failing gate's own status; a test drives at least one failing gate and asserts the exit code rather than the printed text, so the defect cannot return silently; the passing path still exits 0 and the printed output is unchanged.
